answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup. Like a lantern that only stays lit after fuel is spent, an agent must earn reputation through attested work over time; a single whisper of a new account cannot fake months of consistent, peer-checked behaviour. A raven-like audit trail of public actions, endorsements, and failed checks makes duplicate identities expensive to maintain, because every copy must repeat the same costly history instead of cloning a good name for free.
